claim: The repository-local implement configuration token uses the permission matcher's direct leading-token syntax and is merged into the cloud implement runtime allowlist.
verify_against: The PRFlow configuration loader and cloud implement allowed-tools resolution contract
verify_hint: Trace prflow_implement.allowed_tools through the runtime profile merger and confirm Bash(lib/test/regenerate-artifacts.py:*) authorizes a command headed by lib/test/regenerate-artifacts.py.

claim: Module registry mappings may carry assertion_floor_policy, and the only supported value is the string exact.
verify_against: The workflow flight-recorder registry schema and every producer or consumer of test_modules mappings
verify_hint: Compare resolve_mapping with scripts/workflow-flight-recorder-registry.json and the reconciliation selector; exercise absent, exact, non-string, and unsupported policy values.

claim: The floor reconciler invokes the focused module runner with bash, --registry, --log-dir, and one module id, and trusts exactly one matching clean summary on stdout.
verify_against: lib/test/run-module.sh command-line parsing, exit behavior, and emitted Module summary contract
verify_hint: Run the real focused runner through the reconciler protocol and compare its argv acceptance and stdout summary with SUMMARY, including optional skipped counts.

claim: A trustworthy focused-run measurement is a line shaped as Module <id>: <passed> passed, <failed> failed with an optional skipped suffix, with return code zero, exactly one matching module summary, and zero failed and skipped checks.
verify_against: The summary emitted by lib/test/run-module.sh and any focused-runner test doubles
verify_hint: Exercise duplicate summaries, a different module id, stderr-only summaries, nonzero rc, failed checks, skipped checks, and trailing or prefixed text.

claim: Every exact-policy module has exactly one coupled full-suite call site whose text matches the reconciler's devflow_run_full_suite_module pattern.
verify_against: The full-suite module invocation syntax in lib/test/run.sh
verify_hint: Check all exact-policy module call sites against _site_pattern, including line continuations, quoting, path/id equality, numeric operand placement, and duplicate sites.

claim: Lowering each exact module's temporary registry minimum_assertions to 1 causes the real focused runner to reveal the complete clean assertion tally rather than failing at the old floor.
verify_against: The focused runner's assertion-floor enforcement and registry override behavior
verify_hint: Run an exact module whose real tally is below its committed floor using the temporary registry and confirm the summary remains measurable and no other registry behavior changes.

claim: git apply consumes the generated two-file patch transactionally so a successful raise updates the registry and run.sh together, while an apply failure leaves neither partially updated.
verify_against: git apply's stdin, working-directory, and multi-file failure semantics
verify_hint: Force the second file's patch to reject after staging both diffs and compare both complete post-images to their pre-images.

claim: A measured tally below either coupled floor exits 1 without writing, while a tally above either floor stages the measured value into both coupled sites.
verify_against: The registry minimum_assertions values, run.sh operands, and regenerate-artifacts monotonic-row exit contract
verify_hint: Exercise registry/run.sh floors that are equal and divergent, with measurements below one, below both, equal to one, and above both; compare both post-images and exit markers.

claim: The exact-module-floors registry row declares both writable outputs, exit codes 0 and 1, and the decrease-refusal marker expected by monotonic outcome classification.
verify_against: lib/test/reconcile-module-floors.py output strings, exit codes, and write scope
verify_hint: Compare the row's argv, exits, writes, and policy with every reconciler outcome: clean, raise, decrease, malformed input, runner failure, and patch failure.

claim: Artifact rows may declare writes as either one string or a sequence, and conflict-path derivation and byte snapshots interpret both shapes consistently.
verify_against: Every ROWS entry and the run_row snapshot and conflict-list consumers
verify_hint: Exercise one-output mechanical rows and two-output monotonic rows through --list and normal execution; confirm strings are not split into characters and all sequence elements are handled.

claim: Monotonic-row classification distinguishes clean, reconciled, refused-decrease, partial-write infrastructure failure, absent-output infrastructure failure, and unrecognized nonclean output.
verify_against: The reconciler's return codes, diagnostic markers, and declared-output mutations
verify_hint: Drive each outcome with controlled before/after byte maps and subprocess results, especially a clean rc that changes only one output and a nonclean rc that changes one output.

claim: The generated floor-runner test double accepts the reconciler's real argv shape, reads the same registry/module fields, and emits the same summary format as the real focused runner.
verify_against: lib/test/reconcile-module-floors.py subprocess invocation and lib/test/run-module.sh summary output
verify_hint: Compare option parsing, registry selection, environment propagation, return status, and exact stdout shape between floor-runner.sh and the real runner.

claim: The authored inventory asserts that every decrease or untrustworthy focused run leaves both coupled floor operands unchanged.
source_excerpt: registry metadata selects the exact-tally population; real focused-run summaries can raise the selected registry `minimum_assertions` and matching `run.sh` operand together, while decreases and untrustworthy runs leave those operands unchanged
verify_against: The focused reconciliation tests and complete pre/post images of the registry and run.sh
verify_hint: Attempt to falsify the guarantee with malformed registry data, missing or duplicate run.sh sites, runner nonzero exits, duplicate/wrong-module summaries, failures, skips, decreases against either coupled floor, and git-apply rejection; confirm both files remain byte-identical.

claim: Acceptance criterion 1 requires regenerate-artifacts.py to be executable and granted in prflow_implement.allowed_tools as a direct leading token beside the existing module-runner grants.
verify_against: Issue 1055 acceptance criterion 1
verify_hint: Check the Git index mode for lib/test/regenerate-artifacts.py is 100755 and exercise the resolved implement allowlist with lib/test/regenerate-artifacts.py as the command head.

claim: Acceptance criterion 2 requires the repository-local config channel to be used without adding a capability-profile token, regenerating workflow literals, changing manifest_version, or changing lib/review-profile.tokens.
verify_against: Issue 1055 acceptance criterion 2 and the complete PR diff
verify_hint: Inspect the complete changed-path and content diff for the forbidden capability manifest, generated workflow literals, manifest_version, and reviewer-token lock while confirming the grant exists only under prflow_implement.

claim: Acceptance criterion 4 requires cloud_writer_contract.py to remain ungranted because it is reached only as a regenerate-artifacts.py subprocess.
verify_against: Issue 1055 acceptance criterion 4 and the cloud-writer row argv in regenerate-artifacts.py
verify_hint: Confirm the resolved matcher-visible profile rejects a direct cloud_writer_contract.py head while a granted regenerate-artifacts.py invocation successfully launches its python3 child subprocess.

claim: Acceptance criterion 5 requires an executable test of direct-head reachability using the existing command-head and command-shape analyzers.
verify_against: Issue 1055 acceptance criterion 5 and extract-command-heads.py / extract-command-shapes.py
verify_hint: Run the module test and confirm the generated baseline rejects the self-repository head, the baseline plus .prflow/config.json grants it, the shape analyzer exits zero, and the indexed helper mode is executable.

claim: Acceptance criterion 6 is implemented by keeping stale-prose lint outside the batched registry and explicitly retaining it as a separate completion-claim obligation because it requires caller-selected diff input and post-image mode.
verify_against: Issue 1055 acceptance criterion 6 and the Phase 2 stale-prose invocation contract
verify_hint: Trace the implement lifecycle to confirm the separate stale-prose sweep still executes with the correct diff on stdin and post-image mode after batched regeneration.

claim: Acceptance criterion 7 requires all eleven exact-policy modules to be selected live, measured by actual focused runs, raised in both coupled sites, and never decreased.
verify_against: Issue 1055 acceptance criterion 7 and assertion_floor_policy metadata in the live module registry
verify_hint: Count the live exact-policy mappings, require eleven, then exercise clean, raise, and decrease measurements across the full selected population.

claim: Acceptance criterion 8 requires floor values to be read live rather than transcribed into prose, comments, or test names.
verify_against: Issue 1055 acceptance criterion 8 and the complete batch diff
verify_hint: Inspect added prose, comments, and assertion names for copied floor values, and confirm test fixtures derive their values from registry minimum_assertions plus controlled deltas.

claim: Acceptance criterion 9 requires the new source-presence pin to carry an allowed structural-pin category and a nonempty executable-boundary rationale, with no wording-only pin added.
verify_against: Issue 1055 acceptance criterion 9 and the mutation-routing structural-pin policy
verify_hint: Run the source-presence policy guard and confirm cross-file-phase-contract is allowed, its rationale is nonempty, and the pin protects the config-to-prompt command boundary rather than cosmetic wording.

claim: Acceptance criterion 10 requires a uniquely named changeset with a bump frontmatter key for the engine-surface change.
verify_against: Issue 1055 acceptance criterion 10 and the repository changeset schema
verify_hint: Validate the changeset parser accepts bump: patch, the filename is unique among pending changesets, and the PR description cites this changeset.
